batchName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Origins (509-450 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Early Republic: The Conflict of the Orders - Origins (509-450 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What does the Latin word veto mean?
questions.explanation: A tribune who said veto blocked an act of a magistrate or even the Senate.
questions.sourceQuote: From this grew the veto (Latin for "I forbid")

questions.question: What was a secessio plebis?
options: A mass withdrawal of the plebs from Rome
questions.explanation: The plebs left the city together, like a general strike, until their demands were met.
questions.sourceQuote: This tactic became known as a *secessio* (in full *secessio plebis*, "the withdrawal of the plebs")

questions.question: Plebeians filled the ranks of the exercitus. What was it?
questions.explanation: Plebeian soldiers were most of the army, which is why their refusal to fight was so powerful.
questions.sourceQuote: filled the ranks of the army (*exercitus*).

questions.question: What was nexum?
options: A marriage between patricians and plebeians
questions.explanation: A debtor who could not pay could be enslaved: the Romans called this nexum.
questions.sourceQuote: a form of debt bondage the Romans called *nexum*.

questions.question: Plebiscites take their name from the Latin plebiscita. What did it mean?
questions.explanation: Plebiscites were the resolutions of the Plebeian Council; at first they bound only plebeians.
questions.sourceQuote: and passed resolutions called plebiscites (*plebiscita*, "decisions of the plebs").

questions.question: The second board of decemvirs ruled with no provocatio. What was it?
options: The right to vote by tribe
questions.explanation: Without the right of appeal, citizens had no protection against the decemvirs.
questions.sourceQuote: ruling with no tribunes to check them and no right of appeal (*provocatio*).

questions.question: Romans called debt aes alienum. What does it mean, word for word?
questions.explanation: Bronze was Rome’s early money, so a debt was literally bronze that belonged to someone else.

questions.question: In the Twelve Tables, what was the patria potestas?
options: A father’s power over his son
questions.explanation: The Tables limited it: a father who sold his son three times lost his power over him.
questions.sourceQuote: lost his power over him, the *patria potestas* ("power of the father").
